title: Effect of sputtering working pressure on InZnO and InZnMgO thin films and their application to solar cells
authors: Dwinanri Egyna; Yoshihiro Oketou; Shogo Ishizuka; Yukiko Kamikawa; Jiro Nishinaga; Takayuki Negami; Abdurashid Mavlonov; Takashi Minemoto
affiliations: Ritsumeikan University; Ritsumeikan University; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology; Ritsumeikan University; Ritsumeikan University; Ritsumeikan University
abstract: Transparent conductive oxides represent a critical materials platform for modern optoelectronic applications, particularly in photovoltaic devices where the transparent electrode substantially influences device performance parameters. This investigation examined the systematic effects of sputtering working pressure on the structural, optical, and electrical properties of InZnO (IZO) and Mg-doped IZO (IZMO) thin films deposited via radiofrequency magnetron sputtering. Results demonstrate that reducing working pressure enhances carrier mobility from 8.48 to 31.8 cm 2 /V·s and increases carrier concentration while widening optical bandgap. However, the dominant mechanism for bandgap widening differs between the two systems: for IZO, it is primarily attributed to reduced defect states from improved short-range order, while for IZMO, both the Burstein-Moss effect and defect reduction contribute. The Mg-doped variant exhibited superior photovoltaic performance, achieving 18.97% efficiency in Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 solar cells compared to 17.03% for the undoped composition. These findings establish material-specific optimal deposition conditions—with IZMO achieving peak performance at a higher working pressure (1.50 Pa) than IZO (0.25 Pa)—and demonstrate that compositional engineering effectively balances competing optical and electrical properties for enhanced device performance. • Systematic investigation of sputtering pressure effects on InZnO and InZnMgO thin films. • Lower deposition pressure enhances conductivity and widens the optical bandgap. • Mg-doping effectively breaks the inherent trade-off in transparent conductor performance. • InZnMgO based CIGSe solar cells achieved 18.97% PCE, outperforming InZnO.

title: Energy levels analysis of magnetron sputtered MoOx thin films
authors: Nico Ruskaup; Konstantin Kimon Rücker; Kai Gehrke; Stephan J. Heise; Martin Vehse
affiliations: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR); Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR); Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR); Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR); Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)
abstract: Ultrathin molybdenum oxide films are promising as transparent carrier-selective layers in photovoltaic cells, yet the electronic structure of sputtered molybdenum oxide (MoOx) and, therefore, the nature of electronic transport remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we show that magnetron-sputtered MoOx thin films exhibit a largely invariant energy-level structure across variations in thickness, target material, and underlying layer, while remaining electrically nonmetallic. Films with thicknesses of ≈5 nm and ≈20 nm were prepared from either a metallic molybdenum target in a reactive process or a ceramic MoOx target on glass and, for some samples, on germanium or aluminum doped zinc oxide coated glass. The results from Kelvin probe force microscopy, ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy, UV–Vis–NIR spectroscopy, optical modeling, and four-point probe measurements were combined to determine the work function, valence-band edge energy, optical bandgap, and derived conduction-band edge energy. Neither film thickness, target type, nor underlying layer seems to create a clear systematic shift of the energy levels. Additional occupied states were observed at binding energies of about 1.0–1.6 eV and are consistent with defect-related intra-gap states. The Fermi level is found to be ∼0.1–0.5 eV above the conduction-band edge derived from the optical bandgap. The results are discussed with respect to the mechanisms underlying the carrier-selective transport in functional MoOx thin films.

title: Fabrication of all-solid-state thin-film thermal switching devices using Y-Mg thin-film as the thermal switching layer
authors: Yuzo Shigesato; Ryuto Nishimura; Yuki Oguchi; Makoto Kashiwagi
abstract: We fabricated and demonstrated the all-solid-state thermal switch device that uses Y-Mg alloy as the thermal switching layer. The fabricated devices consisted of 7-layers (ITO / Y-Mg / Pd / thin-WO3 / Ta2O5 / WO3 / ITO) deposited on glass or Si-wafer substrates by magnetron sputtering, where the WO3 film as a H+ ion-storage layer, the Ta2O5 film as an ion conductive layer, the Pd film as a catalyst layer, the thin-WO3 film as a leakage barrier layer, and the ITO films as transparent electrodes. The switching of the fabricated device between the metallic (mirror) state and the semiconductor (transparent) state was clearly confirmed by optical measurement. As analyzing by X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, it was confirmed that the structure of the Y-Mg alloy was transformed into YH3-MgH2 by intercalating H+ ions (reduction) with applying negative voltage, and the structure was transformed back to the Y-Mg alloy by ejecting H+ ions (oxidation) with applying positive voltage. The thermal conductivity was evaluated as 3.5 and 1.9 W m-1 K-1 in the metallic and semiconductor states, respectively, and the reversible switching of the thermal conductivity was confirmed.
keywords: hydrogen intercalation; hydrogen storage; WO3; tantalum pentoxide; transparent electrodes; thin film devices; semiconductor-metal transition; all-solid-state devices; magnetron sputtering

title: MAGNETRON DEPOSITION OF TRANSPARENT AZO FILMS FROM COMPOSITE AND SINGLE-ELEMENT TARGETS
authors: Dobrynya V. Kolodko; Andrey V. Kaziev; Dmitry G. Ageychenkov; Aleksandr V. Tumarkin; Maksim M. Kharkov; К. В. Смирнова; Dmitriy A. Shutov
affiliations: Kotelnikov Institute of Radioengineering and Electronics of the Russian Academy of Sciences; National Research Nuclear University MEPhI; National Research Nuclear University MEPhI; National Research Nuclear University MEPhI; National Research Nuclear University MEPhI; MIREA - Russian Technological University; MIREA - Russian Technological University

abstract: Different magnetron deposition approaches have been considered to fabricate transparent conductive coatings based on aluminum-doped zinc oxide (ZnO:Al2O3, AZO) on polymer substrates. In the first method, a single magnetron with a compound ZnO:Al2O3 target was used. The magnetron's magnetic configuration was adjusted to control the ion flux to the substrate. A correlation was established between the electrical resistance of the formed AZO film and the ion flux. The minimum sheet resistance of AZO coatings obtained by this approach was as low as 300 Ω/□. The tunability of the process has been shown to be greatly enhanced by using two independent magnetrons with single-element Zn and Al targets. A novel multilayer coating method was proposed where ZnO layer was formed by sputtering a metallic Zn target in Ar/O2 gas mixture while the alloying layer was deposited by sputtering a metallic Al target in a pure argon atmosphere. The dopant ratio in the resulting AZO structure was controlled by varying the duration of ZnO and Al layer deposition cycles. This approach provided flexible control over the coating's composition. The corresponding samples demonstrated high functional properties, with a surface resistance of 10 Ω/□ and a resistivity of 3×10⁻6 Ω×m coupled with high optical transparency, confirming the coatings’ potential for use in optoelectronic devices. title: Maskless mechanical structuring of thermally annealed ITO electrodes for transparent thin-film transistors
authors: Seung-Hun Lee; Hae-In Hwang; Soeun Choi; A.L. Park; Jihun Ha; Jae Woong Lee; Yeong‐Eun Yoo; Min Hwan Lee; Jeong Hwan Kim
affiliations: University of California, Merced; Hanbat National University; Hanbat National University; Hanbat National University; Hanbat National University; University of California, Merced; Korea Institute of Machinery & Materials; University of California, Merced; Hanbat National University
abstract: This study presents the first application of maskless mechanical microfabrication to indium tin oxide (ITO), a brittle transparent conducting oxide, demonstrating its viability as a patterning strategy for transparent device integration. Unlike conventional photolithography or chemical etching, this approach enables direct, lithography-free structuring of transparent conductors through precision mechanical loading. It eliminates resist- and etchant-based steps, thereby reducing the overall process complexity and mitigating potential etch-induced damage and residue contamination. ITO films (∼100 nm thick), deposited via DC magnetron sputtering, were thermally annealed at 300 °C to enhance machinability. Annealing improved optical transmittance at 550 nm (from 85.7% to 88.3%) and reduced sheet resistance by 63.5%, indicating increased film density and crystallinity. Mechanical loading precisely controlled between 4 and 12 mN enables selective material removal, with complete separation of annealed films achieved at 6 mN. To demonstrate applicability to transparent electronics, ZnO thin-film transistors (TFTs) were fabricated using mechanically defined ITO source/drain electrodes, yielding robust n-type operation with an on/off ratio of 2.4 × 10 6 and channel lengths as short as ∼1.3 μm. This work pioneers mechanical microfabrication for transparent conductive oxide (TCO) films and establishes a lithography-free strategy that is extendable to other TCO materials for next-generation display and electronics applications.

title: Multifractal and optoelectronic evolution of ITO thin films under hydrogen plasma treatment
authors: Hajieh Bastami; Ali Arman; Alireza Grayeli; Sahar Rezaee; Stanislav Jurečka; Talu Stefan; Chandra Kumar; Ram Pratap Yadav; Azizollah Shafiekhani
affiliations: Technical and Vocational University; Sharif University of Technology | Academic Center for Education, Culture and Research; Nuclear Science and Technology Research Institute; Islamic Azad University of Kermanshah; University of Žilina; Technical University of Cluj-Napoca; Universidad Mayor; University of Allahabad; Alzahra University
abstract: This study systematically investigates the influence of hydrogen plasma treatment on indium tin oxide (ITO) thin films deposited via RF magnetron sputtering and subsequently processed by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD). A comprehensive characterization of the structural, roughness, optical, and electrical properties was performed employing X-ray diffraction (XRD), atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), UV-visible spectroscopy, and four-point probe electrical measurements. Results indicate a hydrogen flow rate-dependent preferential crystallographic orientation, with higher flow rates promoting the (222) plane concomitant with hydroxyl bond formation and a reduction in oxygen vacancy concentration. In contrast, lower hydrogen flow rates favor the (400) orientation, indicative of oxygen depletion and increased vacancy density. AFM analyses, incorporating statistical, multifractal, and bearing area methodologies, consistently elucidate the evolution of surface morphology and roughness under varying hydrogen plasma exposure. Optical characterization reveals enhanced transmittance and bandgap widening correlated with prolonged hydrogen treatment. Electrical measurements demonstrate a reduction in sheet resistance associated with increased oxygen vacancies during short-duration hydrogen plasma exposure, whereas extended treatments lead to elevated resistance, attributed to charge carrier scattering by hydroxyl groups. These findings elucidate the complex interplay between hydrogen plasma parameters and ITO thin film properties, providing critical insights for tailoring material performance in optoelectronic and transparent conductive applications.

title: Non-Epitaxial Growth and Electrical Properties of Highly (222)-Oriented ITO Thin Films
authors: Wei Yang; Zhuolin Zhou; Yukai Gao; Liteng Ren; Tong Liu; Guoqiang Li
abstract: The crystallographic orientation of transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) is a critical determinant of their functional properties. Herein, we demonstrate the non-epitaxial growth of highly (222)-oriented indium tin oxide (ITO) films on quartz substrates via magnetron sputtering, mediated by a yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) buffer layer. The YSZ layer not only provides a stable template for preferential ITO growth but also ensures exceptional process robustness. Morphological analysis reveals a quasi-triangular grain morphology and a continuous vertical columnar growth mode throughout the film thickness. Following optimization of an in-situ annealing process, the ITO films exhibit a low resistivity of 1.65×10-4 Ω-cm and a high figure of merit of 0.039 Ω-1. This overall performance surpasses that of commercial ITO benchmarks and most values reported in the literature.
keywords: indium tin oxide; transparent conducting oxides; yttria-stabilized zirconia buffer layer; magnetron sputtering; columnar grain growth; in situ annealing; electrical resistivity; figure of merit; quartz substrate; crystal orientation

title: Preparation and characteristics analysis of resistive random access memory based on samarium - yttrium oxide
authors: Shaobing Shen; Yuanbin Chen; Jin Ren
affiliations: Zhaoqing University; Zhaoqing University; Zhaoqing University
abstract: Abstract RRAM is one of the emerging non-volatile memory types and has been extensively studied due to its advantages, such as a simple structure, fast read/write speeds, strong scalability, and compatibility with CMOS technology. As a semiconductor material, rare earth oxides naturally possess high dielectric constants, high breakdown voltages, high stability, and excellent durability. These materials are indispensable for resistive random access memories (RRAM) and offer broad application prospects. Among them, Samarium oxide exhibits low-power resistive switching behavior, while Yttrium oxide demonstrates superior electrical properties and good stability. In this study, Samarium oxide and Yttrium oxide powders were mixed and subjected to processes including grinding, drying, and high-temperature calcination. Subsequently, a thin film was deposited on an ITO substrate using RF magnetron sputtering technology. Finally, an aluminum electrode was deposited to fabricate an RRAM thin-film device with the structure of ITO/SmYO 3 /Al. XRD analysis was conducted to confirm the crystalline phase and powder composition of the thin film, AFM measurements were performed to evaluate surface roughness, and I-V characterization revealed that the thin film exhibited excellent resistive switching characteristics and bipolar resistive switching behavior.
keywords: resistive random access memory; rare earth oxides; resistive switching; bipolar resistive switching; non-volatile memory; thin film devices; RF magnetron sputtering; high-temperature calcination; dielectric constant

title: P‐.9.8: One Electromagnetic Shielding and Anti‐reflective LCD Module based on Magnetron Sputtered Optical Glass
authors: Gang Liu; Chunlin Xi; Xinxiang Zhu; Yongmei Luo; Zeyuan Zhang
journal: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers
abstract: Airborne liquid crystal display (LCD) devices require high electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and strong light visibility [1] . The former is mainly to achieve reliable information interaction of aircraft in electronic countermeasures, while the latter is to ensure information readability in high‐brightness environments up to 100,000 lux [2] . Ruggedized LCD is currently the main technical implementation method for airborne displays. It achieves electromagnetic shielding and anti‐reflection functions respectively by attaching optical functional glass with AR film to the upper layer of the LCD panel and optical functional glass with ITO shielding film to the lower layer. This technical solution increases the power consumption, weight, thickness, and cost of the device. This paper proposes an airborne LCD module based on magnetron sputtered coated optical glass with high Transmittance (full‐Spectrum transmittance＞92%). By coating AR film and ITO film on both sides of the optical glass respectively, the three‐in‐one function of anti‐reflection (reflectivity＜0.4%), electromagnetic shielding (SE ＞ 45 db), and ruggedization is realized. This LCD module has certain advantages in power consumption, product weight and thickness, and design cost.
keywords: LCD display; electromagnetic interference shielding; antireflection coatings; electromagnetic compatibility; optical transmittance; aircraft displays

title: Reducing the noble metal and titanium content of anode PTLs in PEM water electrolysis - performance and degradation
authors: Sarah Zerressen
affiliations: Forschungszentrum Jülich
abstract: Among the industrialized processes of water electrolysis, proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) has been demonstrated to exhibit high efficiency, thus contributing to the production of green hydrogen and playing a crucial role in decarbonizing the production of fundamental chemicals such as ammonia and methanol. Additionally, PEMWE can contribute to the electrification of our energy system, a pivotal step in the transition to a low-carbon economy. Nonetheless, the financial outlay required for this undertaking is substantial, primarily due to the employment of noble metal catalysts and noble metal-coated titanium porous transport layers (PTLs). Therefore, this work investigated two approaches to reduce the use of precious metals on PTLs and the reduction of titanium as a base material. The first approach involved noble metal free coating materials for the anode PTL, which have not yet been researched as PTL coatings or have been investigated with inconsistent results. The materials involved titanium nitride, tungsten, indium tin oxide, niobium, tantalum and titanium-niobium and titanium-tantalum alloys. Their deposition was carried out by the institute IMD-2 using physical vapor deposition (magnetron sputtering) and thermal spray techniques (atmospheric and vacuum plasma spraying as well as cold gas spraying). While magnetron sputtering provided dense and thin coatings of just a few micrometers, thermal spray processes yielded thicker coatings between 30 μm and 60 μm. The coated PTLs were investigated for their stability in PEMWE single cell operation using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), ex-situ resistance measurements and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with elemental analysis via energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The experiments revealed, that almost all materials underwent oxidation, resulting in increased ohmic resistances and decreased cell performances. Only coatings consisting of a mixture of 6 at.% niobium or tantalum and 94 at.% titanium provided a significant enhanced stability over 144 h. However, also pure magnetron-sputtered Ti layers enabled stable PEMWE performance close to the alloy coating. Hence, the influence of niobium and tantalum in the titanium layer on the preservation of the conductivity of the forming oxide scale has not yet been conclusively proven. Due to the insufficient oxidation stability of the materials that were selected based on their reported corrosion stability under simulated PEMWE conditions in the literature, additional investigations addressed the question to what extent ex-situ corrosion tests can reflect the oxidation and corrosion stability of anode PTL coatings. For rapidly oxidizing TiN coatings, it was found that the conditions set in the corrosion cell (pH 1.16 and potentials of 1.4 V and 1.6 V vs. RHE) led to stronger oxidation than for coatings in PEMWE experiments at 1.5 V and 2.0 V cell voltage. Consequently, it was found, that ex situ tests under the conditions most commonly used in the literature to date (sulfuric acid and potentials up to 2.0 V) are not adequate for simulating the oxidation of PTL coatings. The second approach aiming for reduction of the amount of Ti used consisted of titanium-reduced and stainless steel-based anode PTLs as an alternative to full titanium PTLs. As stainless steel requires a corrosion protection layer, magnetron sputtered (PVD) layers with a thickness <10 μm were deposited on stainless steel meshes and felts and cold gas sprayed (CGS) Ti layers with a thickness between 33 ± 14 μm and 60 ± 12 μm on meshes. The results with thin coatings on the two different substrates differed greatly. While the mesh showed extensive pitting corrosion, the felt PTL was only subject to surface corrosion with increasing cell performance even after more than 1000 h of operation, whereby membrane thinning could not be ruled out, explaining a substantial part of the performance improvement. As the two substrates were provided by different suppliers, they exhibited slightly different proportions of alloying elements. Consequently, the results indicate a correlation between stainless steel composition and corrosion resistance, requiring further systematic research. Sufficient corrosion protection of the 316L mesh-based PTLs was only achieved with a 60 ± 16 μm thick CGS titanium coating (CG-60). During the experiments, the effluent water from the anode and cathode sides was screened for emission of stainless steel components via inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). With thinner CGS Ti layers (48 ± 16 μm and 33 ± 16 μm), increased emission of stainless steel components was observed, underscoring superior corrosion protection provided by the thicker coating. All Ti-coated stainless steel substrates had to be sputtered with an additional 38 nm Pt contact layer to prevent titanium oxidation, enabling the CG-60 PTLs to achieve comparable performance and stability over 1000 h at 2.0 V cell voltage to commercial Pt-coated Ti felt PTLs while saving approximately 25 % titanium. Finally, performance data were extracted from dynamic wind profile operation of PEMWE single cells with state-of-the-art PTLs, providing a starting point for the analysis of PEMWE cells with new components. The methods developed for this purpose allow characterization during dynamic operation without having to interrupt the operation to record I-V curves or impedance spectra. Theextracted performance indicators include cell voltage changes, I-V curves and ohmic resistances as well as indications of changes in catalyst activity.
keywords: proton exchange membrane water electrolysis; titanium anode; titanium nitride; titanium-niobium alloys; coating oxidation; corrosion resistance; ohmic resistance; green hydrogen production; magnetron sputtering; plasma spraying; cold spray; electrochemical impedance spectroscopy

title: Role of Hydrogen on the ITO/Ag Contact Resistance for Low-Temperature Screen-Printing Metallization of Pero/Si Tandems
authors: Jannik N. Kleesiek; Maximilian Günther; Alexander Steigert; Darja Erfurt; Stefan Janke; Marlene Härtel; Rutger Schlatmann; Bernd Stannowski; Angelika Harter
abstract: The upscaling of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells is an increasingly important topic in research to bridge the gap between laboratory scale performance and industrial application. This requires adapting well-established technologies to enable the processing of upscaled tandem cell manufacturing steps, including the transparent conductive oxide (TCO) front electrode by magnetron sputtering and the metal contact by screen printing. For state-of-the-art silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells, both the TCO and the metal contact are annealed at temperatures around 200 °C. Perovskite films in contrast are known to degrade at such high temperatures, which makes the processing of the front contact for perovskite based solar cells more challenging. In this work, we demonstrate an optimized screen-printing process that, with the right choice of sputtering process parameters, enables a low TCO/Ag contact resistivity of around 1 mΩcm2at a maximum processing temperature of 135 °C and therefore suitable for (most) perovskite absorbers. The interaction between the TCO and the silver paste is analyzed in detail with respect to achieving low contact resistivity between the two layers. Our results demonstrate that controlling the hydrogen content during the sputtering process is critical: higher hydrogen levels result in a clear increase in the specific contact resistivity. Finally, we show a screen-printed tandem device that further confirms the process feasibility.
keywords: perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells; screen printing; silver paste; hydrogen content; sputtering parameters; transparent conducting oxides; low-temperature metallization; silicon heterojunction solar cells; perovskite degradation; contact resistivity

title: Sputter-resistant aluminium oxide layer enables robust perovskite tandem solar cells
authors: Seyma Topcu; Nepomuk Zieske; Mayank Kedia; Chittaranjan Das; Martina Pesci; Oleksandr B. Bondarchuk; José J. Jerónimo-Rendon; Tobias Heim; Bhaskar Singh; Marion Dussouillez; Bekele Hailegnaw; Asfaw Negash; Matteo Schilirò; Stefan A. L. Weber; Stephanie Essig; Michael Saliba
affiliations: University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart | Forschungszentrum Jülich; University of Stuttgart | Forschungszentrum Jülich; University of Stuttgart; International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory; University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart; ; ; University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart; University of Stuttgart | Forschungszentrum Jülich
abstract: Protective buffer layers are a key strategy to facilitate the sputter deposition of transparent front electrodes in semi-transparent perovskite and highly efficient perovskite tandem solar cells. Here, we explore a thin aluminium oxide (AlO x ) layer, deposited through atomic layer deposition (ALD), as a buffer layer between the established C 60 electron transport layer and sputtered indium tin oxide (ITO) contact in a “p-i-n” (inverted) device architecture. By using multimodal spectroscopic methods, we compare AlO x to the more widely employed SnO x . Although ALD is known as a conformal process, we find that the growth of SnO x (<20 nm) on the C 60 layer frequently results in pinholes, whereas ∼ 3–5 nm-thin layers of AlO x allow for a more homogeneous coverage. The presence of in-gap states revealed in the wide-bandgap alumina buffer layer enables efficient charge extraction. Under low-power magnetron sputtering conditions, a 3 nm AlO x buffer layer effectively suppresses sputtering-induced damage, whereas a 1.5 nm AlO x layer does not. Devices with 3 nm AlO x perform similarly to those with 20 nm SnO x , with power conversion efficiencies exceeding 17% for semi-transparent perovskite and 26% for perovskite/silicon tandem devices. Thus, we conclude the suitability of thin AlO x as a sputter-resistant buffer layer offering the advantage of a dense and uniform ALD process, reduced material consumption, and a faster fabrication process for future perovskite tandem and semi-transparent devices.

title: Synergistic optimization of oxygen stoichiometry and thermal annealing in ITO/Ag/ITO multilayer transparent conductive films for high-performance optoelectronic applications
authors: Guolu Liu; H Liu; Weiming Liu; Xiaofeng Zhang; Yue Yan
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials; Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials; ; ; Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials
journal: Journal of Science Advanced Materials and Devices
abstract: ITO/Ag/ITO (IAI) multilayer transparent conductive films (TCFs) were fabricated by reactive magnetron sputtering under designed Ar/O 2 gas flow ratios and annealed up to 300 °C for 30 min in air. The results show that the optimized films with a 10 nm Ag interlayer, deposited under high appropriate oxygen flow (Ar/O 2 ∼30/2) and annealed at 300 °C for 30 min in air, achieved a sheet resistance of ∼7 Ω/sq. and >90% average visible transmittance (peak 90.3% at 550 nm with substrate included). X-ray reflectivity and diffraction revealed that annealing induces Ag and ITO crystallization, and interfacial smoothing, which results in improvements in conductivity and transparency. Moreover, the favorable optical constants of oxygen-rich ITO, which act as effective anti-reflection layers, are key factors for producing IAI TCFs with high transparency. These results demonstrate that synergistic control of oxygen stoichiometry and thermal annealing enables IAI TCFs to outperform conventional single-layer ITO, offering a promising route for high-performance transparent electrodes.

title: Systematic Optimization of Sputtered AZO Thin Films and Their Integration as Alternative Transparent Electrodes for Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Zeynep Mavili; Mücahit Yılmaz
affiliations: Necmettin Erbakan University; Necmettin Erbakan University
abstract: Abstract Transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) are critical components of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), motivating the search for low-cost and scalable alternatives to conventional fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO). Among the proposed alternatives, Al-doped ZnO (AZO) has been widely investigated as a low-cost, indium-free transparent conductive oxide. However, systematic studies correlating sputtering parameters with AZO thin film properties and PSC performance through direct benchmarking against commercial FTO under identical device fabrication conditions remain limited. In this study, AZO thin films were systematically optimized by magnetron sputtering through controlled variation of sputtering power, annealing conditions, substrate temperature, and deposition duration. The optimized high-temperature-grown AZO film (AZO-13) exhibited high visible transparency (∼86%), low sheet resistance (1.26 × 101 Ω·sq–1), strong preferential (002) orientation, and high calculated electrical conductivity (∼9.85 × 102 S·cm–1), achieving a Haacke figure of merit (0.668) that slightly surpassed that of commercial FTO (0.664). To evaluate its applicability as a transparent electrode, the optimized AZO film was directly integrated into PSC devices and compared with commercial FTO under identical fabrication conditions. The AZO-based PSC achieved a stabilized efficiency of 16.49%, while comparative PL/TRPL, EQE, and EIS analyses revealed that the lower device performance mainly originated from increased interfacial resistance and less efficient charge extraction. In addition, AZO exhibited improved long-wavelength transparency compared with FTO, suggesting potential relevance for tandem-oriented photovoltaic applications. These results establish a clear process–structure–property–device relationship for sputtered AZO thin films and demonstrate their potential as alternative TCO electrodes for PSC technologies.
keywords: Al-doped ZnO; transparent conducting oxides; perovskite solar cells; sputtering process optimization; sheet resistance; (002) preferred orientation; interfacial resistance; charge extraction

title: Tailoring electro-optical properties of ZnO/Ag/ZnO multilayers by low-energy carbon ion implantation
authors: Sumitra Choudhary; Vikas Sharma; Asokan Kandasami; Abhishek Kumar Sharma
affiliations: JECRC University; Hebrew University of Jerusalem | Malaviya National Institute of Technology Jaipur; University of Petroleum and Energy Studies; JECRC University
abstract: This study explores defect-mediated tuning of electro-optical properties in ZnO/Ag/ZnO (ZAZ) oxide/metal/oxide multilayer thin films via low-energy (100 keV) carbon ion implantation. The multilayers (35 nm/10 nm/35 nm) were deposited on glass substrates using RF magnetron sputtering at room temperature, followed by implantation at fluences ranging from 1×10¹³ to 1×10¹⁶ ions/cm². SRIM/TRIM simulations, incorporating the full multilayer architecture, reveal a projected ion range of ~39.4 nm with significant lateral (~88.3 nm) and radial (~119 nm) straggling, indicating that collision cascades span the entire structure. Energy loss analysis shows dominant electronic stopping (~81%) with a smaller nuclear stopping contribution (~19%) responsible for displacement damage. The simulated defect profile exhibits a broad depth distribution, with an average of ~151.7 vacancies generated per ion, leading to increased dislocation density. Structural characterization confirms retention of the wurtzite ZnO phase with strong (002) orientation, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicates modification of oxygen-related defect states. Electrical measurements demonstrate a non-monotonic response: moderate implantation improves charge transport, reducing sheet resistance from 27.48 Ω/□ (pristine) to 13.44 Ω/□ at 1×10¹⁵ ions/cm² and enhances Hall mobility to 12.28 cm²V⁻¹s⁻¹. At higher fluences, excessive defect accumulation increases carrier scattering, degrading performance and indicating a defect-density threshold. Optical analysis shows visible transmittance of ~73–77%, highlighting the trade-off between transparency and conductivity. Overall, the results establish ion implantation as an effective post-deposition strategy for controlled defect engineering in transparent conducting multilayer films.
keywords: carbon ion implantation; defect engineering; transparent conducting oxides; electro-optical properties; ion straggling; vacancy defects; dislocation density; sheet resistance; Hall mobility; implantation fluence; visible transmittance

title: Thermally intermixed ZnO-rich-to-ITO-rich vertical gradient channels for near-zero-threshold oxide thin-film transistors
authors: Zahid Hassan; Archana T. Anilkumar; Praveen Kumar Sekhar
affiliations: Washington State University Vancouver; Washington State University Vancouver; Washington State University Vancouver
abstract: Balancing carrier transport, electrostatic control, and operational stability remains a central challenge in oxide thin-film transistors (TFTs). Here, a 20 nm vertically composition-graded indium tin oxide (ITO)/ZnO channel was developed with a ZnO-rich region adjacent to the gate dielectric and a progressively increasing ITO fraction toward the source/drain contacts. The channel was fabricated by sequential RF magnetron sputtering followed by annealing at 350C. Cross-sectional TEM and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analyses revealed a continuous, compositionally intermixed oxide film retaining the intended depth-dependent Zn/In distribution, while x-ray diffraction and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a nanocrystalline metal-oxygen network containing defect-related oxygen states. The resulting TFTs exhibited near-zero-threshold enhancement-mode operation with a threshold voltage of 0.18 V, anratio exceeding, a hysteresis of 0.2 V, and a maximum effective field-effect mobility ofcm V sacross five devices. title: Tuning the epsilon near zero wavelength of ITO in the near-IR spectral region via post-process free sputtering
authors: Iman Alhamdan; Aritra S Nomany; Sebastian A. Schulz
affiliations: University of St Andrews; University of Waterloo; University of St Andrews
abstract: Abstract Indium tin oxide (ITO) has become an important material in photonics due to its transparency, high electrical conductivity, and, more recently, its epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) properties for nonlinear optics. In this work, we present a single-step RF magnetron sputtering protocol optimised for hybrid-ENZ metasurfaces, enabling precise tuning of the ENZ wavelength ( λ ENZ ) across 1130–1700+ nm without post-deposition annealing. Through deposition runs across two RF sputtering systems, we systematically explore the effects of film thickness, substrate temperature, and background gas composition on the optical properties of ITO, offering an ITO recipe development protocol for fabricating ENZ-tuned films suitable for advanced nonlinear optical and metasurface devices.
